subjects.abiding-in-his-presence: AIRY coverage, 20–35% ink: most of the frame is quiet warm cream carrying only faint printed atmosphere and earth tone; no background figures or filler detail. Ground the form in real grapevine anatomy: one mature trunk and cordon rooted naturally in vineyard earth, with a fruiting cane growing continuously from a real node. Conceptual device: a narrow golden current of sap is visible inside that naturally attached living cane and reaches its leaves and grapes, while one genuinely pruned cane lies dry on the ground below. No graft union, splice, pipe joint, symmetrical emblem or floating botanical specimen.

subjects.rekindled: COMPOSITION GEOMETRY — BUILD THE FRAME TO THESE NUMBERS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. 70% of this frame is near-solid deep cobalt ink carrying ONLY fine halftone dot texture and NO describable detail — no scenery, no objects, no texture you could name. It is printed, but it is empty. The lit area is SMALL: one small clay oil lamp with a live flame sits low and hard LEFT at roughly 25% across and 70% down. Its light reaches only about an arm's length. Value falls from lit to solid dark within a short distance — there is almost NO broad mid-tone region. Camera is at the height of the ledge itself, level, static, no tilt.  Ground it in real oil-lamp physics: a wheel-made clay lamp, wick through a pinched spout. Conceptual device: the light crosses the empty dark and just reaches a second, UNLIT clay lamp at roughly 75% across, which is dimly visible and nothing else is. MOTION — this becomes a cinemagraph, so exactly ONE thing moves: the lamp flame, moving guttering and leaning. Everything else is a hard static anchor: both lamps, the ledge. No candles, no glass, no text, no glow bloom.
subjects.rekindled-day1-lead: COMPOSITION GEOMETRY — BUILD THE FRAME TO THESE NUMBERS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. 60% of this frame is near-solid deep cobalt ink carrying ONLY fine halftone dot texture and NO describable detail — no scenery, no objects, no texture you could name. Value falls from lit to solid dark within a short distance — there is almost NO broad mid-tone region. Camera is close in at the height of the writing surface, level, static, no tilt.  Ground it in real scribal physics: a hide scroll, a reed pen. Hands enter from the RIGHT edge, seen from the BACK of the hand in near-profile so the fingers are separate and individually countable — EXACTLY four fingers plus one thumb per hand, no overlapping tangle, no top-down cluster. Conceptual device: the light source is behind the page, never in frame. MOTION — this becomes a cinemagraph, so exactly ONE thing moves: the light behind the parchment, moving swelling brighter and dimmer. Everything else is a hard static anchor: the hands, every finger, the pen, the scroll. Scroll stays COMPLETELY BLANK. No letters. No sixth digit, no fused fingers, no glow bloom.

subjects.rekindled-day3-lead: MID coverage, 45-60% ink. Roughly half the frame is quiet printed dark carrying only dot texture; the rest is lit. Do NOT flood the frame with solid ink, and do NOT leave large areas of blank cream. SUBJECT: a close view of ONE human hand seen from the SIDE in strict profile, entering from the right, holding a broken shard of fired clay. Resting in the clay shard is a single small live ember - cracked orange crust over grey ash. ANATOMY IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS IMAGE: exactly ONE hand. Exactly FIVE digits - four fingers plus one thumb. Because the hand is in strict side profile, the fingers are seen edge-on and stack in a clear readable row, each one separate and individually countable against the dark. Middle finger longest, little finger shortest, thumb low on the inner palm. Fingers gently curled around the shard, never fanned, never splayed, never overlapping into a mass. NO second hand anywhere. NO sixth digit. NO fused or webbed fingers. NO cupped top-down view - that pose hides the count and is forbidden here. The ember rests on the CLAY, never on bare skin, because a live coal in a bare palm is physically wrong. The hand is Middle Eastern Semitic: brown to deep brown skin rendered in DENSE blue halftone, clearly darker in value than the cream paper, never left as bare paper. LIGHT: the ember is the only light source and is physically tiny. It catches the fingertips, the near knuckles and the near lip of the clay shard, and nothing else. Falloff is achieved ONLY by increasing halftone dot density - there is absolutely NO soft glow, NO halo, NO bloom, NO haze around the ember. Riso duotone: deep cobalt on warm cream, Ben-Day dots carrying every tone, paper grain, faint crimson misregistration, no greys, full bleed to all four edges, no border. No text or invented glyphs.

MOTION — this becomes a cinemagraph, so exactly ONE thing moves: the flame and its smoke, moving rising and leaning to one side. subjects.rekindled-day5-mid: MID coverage, 45-60% ink. This must NOT look like a catalogue photograph or a product shot. CAMERA: place the lens BELOW the height of the surface, so the edge of the earthen ledge cuts across the frame as a low horizon and you are looking slightly UP at the objects against the dark behind them. Everything above that ledge line falls away into quiet printed dark. Never a flat straight-on eye-level view. LIGHT: one hard raking key from the LEFT, low and close, so each object throws a long shadow to the right and the far sides of the objects are lost in dark. SUBJECT: ten small wheel-made clay oil lamps on packed earth. They are hand-made and must look it - OBVIOUSLY VARIED in size, height, belly shape and spout angle, some squat, some taller, some chipped, some tilted where the ground is uneven. Set them at DELIBERATELY UNEVEN intervals: two nearly touching, a wide gap, three loosely clustered, another gap. Never a regular row, never even spacing, never identical repeated shapes. CONCEPTUAL DEVICE: nine of the wicks are dark or trailing a thin thread of smoke from having just gone out. Exactly ONE still carries a small live flame, positioned about a fifth of the way in from the left, and that single lamp is the only object in the frame casting a clear shadow. Riso duotone: deep cobalt on warm cream, Ben-Day dots carrying every tone, paper grain, faint crimson misregistration, no greys, full bleed to all four edges, no border. No figures, no hands, no candles, no glass, no text.
subjects.rekindled-day5-end: COMPOSITION GEOMETRY — BUILD THE FRAME TO THESE NUMBERS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. 78% of this frame is near-solid deep cobalt ink carrying ONLY fine halftone dot texture and NO describable detail — no scenery, no objects, no texture you could name. Value falls from lit to solid dark within a short distance — there is almost NO broad mid-tone region. Camera is low and close, at the height of the press bed, level, static, no tilt.  Ground it in real machinery and anatomy: a stone crushing wheel on its axle, woven pressing baskets, olive pulp with real texture, and the hands and forearms of a Middle Eastern Semitic worker pressing down with visible strain — hands seen from the SIDE so fingers are countable, EXACTLY four fingers plus a thumb each. Conceptual device: the one bright thing in the frame is the product of the heaviest work in it. subjects.all-these-things: MID-DENSE coverage, 55-65% ink: a dynamic over-the-shoulder view from BEHIND and slightly above three men on a rocky desert hilltop at Rephidim, looking past them and steeply DOWN into the valley where a battle is being fought. FOREGROUND, seen entirely FROM THE BACK, close and large in frame, occupying the lower left and centre: Moses seated on a single rough stone, shoulders and back toward the viewer, both arms raised high above his head, gripping a long plain wooden staff — the rod of God — held horizontally aloft in both hands. Aaron and Hur stand one on each side, also seen from behind, each bracing one of Moses' raised forearms with both hands, their own shoulders dropped and braced under the strain, feet planted wide on the rock. All three wear rough woven Bronze Age tunics and mantles; their backs, necks and the sides of their heads are what the viewer sees, no faces turned to camera. MIDDLE DISTANCE, framed in the gap between Moses' raised arms and past his right shoulder: the battle in the valley floor far below — small distant Israelite and Amalekite foot soldiers in loose ragged lines, bronze-age spears and short swords and hide shields, dust rising, rendered SMALL and low-contrast so the scale reads as genuinely distant. No modern weapons, no horses in armour, no banners with symbols. Conceptual device: the raised staff and the two bracing men form one continuous supported shape in the foreground, and the battle's outcome is visibly tied to it — the line of the staff points out over the valley. The strain is visible in the SUPPORTERS, not the supported. One small warm golden-yellow accent only: the low sun sitting on the far horizon beyond the valley, going down, throwing one decisive raking light direction across the hilltop rock and casting the three men's long shadows back toward the viewer. Hands are critical and must be exact: Moses' two hands wrapped around the staff shaft with five fingers each and visible knuckles; Aaron's and Hur's hands gripping forearm and wrist. Seen from behind, so palms are away from the viewer. Deep perspective and steep foreshortening from the high vantage — near figures large, valley far below and small. No Escher geometry, no floating elements, no symmetrical arrangement; the three figures are irregularly spaced and the composition is asymmetric with the valley opening to one side.
